summary: Pulsar 2849 is a dice-drafting space euro where players draft dice from a shared communal pool to fuel technology, exploration, and infrastructure tracks. It offers multiple parallel paths to victory and rewards efficient engine-building over an eight-round arc.
praised: Clever dice-drafting mechanism where die value and color both matter
Multiple distinct paths to victory keep games varied
Satisfying engine-building feel with tech tree upgrades
Elegant, tight ruleset for the depth it offers
criticised: Can feel dry and heavily systems-focused with little theme
Some strategies (e.g., certain tech combos) seen as stronger in analysis
Dice availability can feel swingy if the pool doesn't favor your plan
Player interaction is fairly indirect for some tastes

interaction.detail: Players draft from the same rolled pool of dice each round, so taking a die denies it to others and can shift what's left, plus a shared map has limited pulsar/planet spots to claim. Beyond that, each player develops their own tech and production engine independently.

sources: end-game set/conversion bonuses from planets and pulsars
scoring.how_you_win: Across the game's fixed 8 rounds, accumulate the most points by advancing technology tracks and collecting/converting planet and pulsar tiles into victory points.
